newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sour crude stays firm as market retreats.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sour crude stays firm as market retreats.

text.p: U.S. sour crude differentials remained firm Tuesday afternoon as outright prices retreated, with traders citing a number of regional disruptions for the sector's relative strength.
West Texas Sour/Midland traded up as high as $2.10 below marker West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, compared with $2.20 on Monday and $2.30 on Friday.

Traders said the closure of two Mexican crude ports for the past four days, delaying at least two large shipments of Maya, as well as temporary problems at the Mars production platform in the Gulf of Mexico, were the main factors.
Earlier Monday, officials at Dos Bocas and Pajaritos said the two crude exporting ports would remain shut on Tuesday and likely through Wednesday becauseo of high winds.
There were two ships waiting to load a total of two million barrels of Maya heavy crude at Dos Bocas, while five tankers were waiting to load and a further four to sail from Parajitos.

Meanwhile, Shell Oil Co said Tuesday that it was gradually bringing production back up at its Mars field in deepwater Gulf of Mexico after an electrical glitch shut production over the weekend. The field had been operating at 86,000 barrels per day.
Also, traders mentioned a threatened strike by pilots guiding tankers in and out of Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela's oil region.
However, WTS/Midland has been firming gradually for some weeks from discounts as deep as $2.80 after sinking sharply since the start of the year.
Eugnene Island also was firmer by 10/15 cents to around $2.15-10 a barrel, though little trade was seen.
In the broader market prices were topsy-turvy Tuesday as WTI futures moved up to a high of $20.09 and down to a low of $19.59 during the day.
On the sweet grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was around minus 32-27 cents a barrel, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was pegged around minus $1.10 a barrel.
WTI/Midland was at minus 31-28 cents a barrel.
Activity was minimal as traders wrap up May activity.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $19.90-20.00 a barrel, up around five cents from late Monday's cash market in line with a funds-generated rise on NYMEX.
The May/June WTYI spread was around two/three cents backwardated, down from 10 or more on Monday, ahead of next Tuesday's expiry.
